headline: Data Scientist Salary in the UK 2026: Average Pay by Level and City
metaDescription: Data scientist salary UK 2026: London average GBP 61,500, junior 36k-47k, lead roles near 98k, top-paying employers and the skills that raise pay.

sections.content:
Data scientists in London earn around £61,500 a year on average in 2026, according to Glassdoor's September data drawn from more than 5,700 salaries. The typical range runs from about £46,600 at the 25th percentile to £83,300 at the 75th percentile, with top earners approaching £112,800. Indeed's August 2026 postings paint a similar picture: £63,545 in London and £62,973 across Greater London, roughly 13 to 14 percent above the national average.

The spread is the story. Data science covers everything from dashboard-building analysts to machine learning engineers shipping production models, and pay follows the complexity of the work. Candidates who can point to deployed models and measurable business impact consistently land above the median, while those in reporting-heavy roles cluster below it.
sections.title: Average Data Scientist Pay in the UK for 2026

sections.content:
Indeed's August 2026 data puts junior data scientists at around £36,200 a year, with interns near £33,400. The first few years are where the curve is steepest — Glassdoor's trend data shows junior data scientists starting slightly above the national average and moving well above it within a few years as their modelling and engineering skills compound.

At the top of the ladder, lead data scientists average around £98,400, principals near £89,700, chief data scientists about £121,600 and directors of data science roughly £138,300. The gap between a strong senior and a lead is largely about ownership: leading projects, mentoring, and responsibility for models that drive revenue.
sections.title: Pay by Seniority: Junior to Director

sections.content:
London dominates UK data science pay, but the capital is not uniform. Indeed's data highlights Hounslow at about £102,700 a year, West London at £91,600 and Uxbridge at £91,300 as the highest-paying pockets — figures that reflect where large corporate and tech employers cluster rather than the postcodes themselves.

Outside London, pay drops but so does the cost of living, and remote-friendly employers increasingly pay London-adjacent salaries nationwide. When comparing offers, weigh total compensation and flexibility alongside the base: a remote role at £70,000 can beat a London role at £80,000 once commuting and rent are accounted for.
sections.title: Where Data Scientists Earn the Most

sections.content:
The skills that command the biggest premiums are the ones closest to production: machine learning engineering, MLOps, and deploying models at scale. Employers pay most for people who ship, because a model in production generates value while a notebook does not. Cloud platforms, experiment tracking and solid statistical foundations underpin all of it.

Domain expertise is the other lever. Data scientists who understand financial risk, healthcare operations or e-commerce funnels access specialist roles with far less competition. Combined with a portfolio of real projects and clear communication of results to non-technical stakeholders, domain knowledge is what separates the £60,000 data scientist from the £100,000 one.
